items.title: Worthia "Showboy" Thomas Interview, 1961-12-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...he wrote to old man Moe. ... [INTERVIEWEE] And that's all I knew then at that time was Professor Randolph.

ctx.x: Or how? Well, at that time, the most playing that we done in that band was the music we played for the show, for the performers. And well this professor, Professor Randolph, he had pretty good ideas about jazz then at that time, because he was writing some arrangements, that is, for the bands to do specialists. Had special spots along during the show that the band would do specialists. Well he had wrote some nice stuff for a band to do specialists.

Roofing Randolph, I forget his first name, had worked with Louis Armstrong later, and he wrote to old man Moe. He says, Randolph, I used to hear him in Chicago. He'd been with Armstrong for a while, sort of organized his band, played second trumpet with him. Well this Randolph was a violin player. Oh no, this was a trumpet player.

And that's all I knew then at that time was Professor Randolph. Well it might be a relative of his, that's what you're thinking of. Well he's from Chicago. But he had pretty good ideas, that is, of writing swing music at that time, because he used to write some nice stuff, that is, for overtures. And along by the middle way of the show we had certain numbers we would do, the band would do. Well he would write those himself. And they were somewhat on time, at that time.
